mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation index above 3% over the next month raises expectations of future rate hikes, which compresses equity discount rates and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when inflation exceeds 3% for the next month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 monthly increases, signaling labor market strength that supports corporate earnings growth and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 in the next 60 trading days
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS > 200,000 for the horizon (mean ratio < 1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (household spending) of at least 5% over the next 20 days predicts increased consumer confidence and higher corporate earnings, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥5% over the next 20 trading days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the 5% HOUST increase (p-value > 0.05 in out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) index below 95.0 for two consecutive months triggers a supply-side shock that raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite INDPRO contraction (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 5% for 3 months indicates labor market slack, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady longer than expected, which supports equity valuations and produces positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE < 5% for 3 months (out-of-sample).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both PAYEMS and RSAFS (retail and services activity) by more than 10% over the next 20 days suggests a dual slowdown that dampens earnings expectations and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < -10% AND RSAFS < -10% over the next 20 trading days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the combined decline in PAYEMS and RSAFS (interaction effect significant at p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for the next month signals aggressive policy tightening, which increases real borrowing costs and reduces equity discounting, producing negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in GDPC1 (GDP momentum) of at least 2% over the next 60 days is interpreted as a weakening economic momentum that raises uncertainty and compresses valuations, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% over the next 60 trading days
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite GDPC1 decline (t-test p > 0.05).
